column1: #   type: 'm' mail, 'r' request, another character keeps the name.
#   The C code takes the path of a queue entry and the port takes the name of
#   a file, so the cases hold a name without a directory.
#   The week of an arcmail name holds the case of every boundary: the days 0
#   to 6 answer the letters of the week, the day 7, a first character below
#   '0' (the '-' case; a '/' or a '.' of a path would not reach the port,
#   because the C code takes the name of the file from the path), a second
#   character that is no '#', an extension of 2 or of 4 characters, an
#   extension of 3 characters with a letter, an empty extension, and a name
#   without a dot hold no case.
#   The random names of the mail and of the request hold no case, because
#   the C code answers the time and the sequence of rand().
# See tests/README.md for the field format.
